text: This lab runs an actual fair benchmark, end to end, across four methods -- brute force, greedy local search, simulated annealing, and simulated QAOA -- on the two graphs you've used throughout this course. The goal is applying Lesson 21's fairness checklist to your own results.

On Instance A, the 4-cycle with true optimum 4, QAOA at depth 1 achieves an expected cost of only 2.9996, a ratio of 0.75 -- but sampling from its actual measurement distribution tells a more encouraging story. The two optimal bitstrings together carry about 53% of the probability, so the true optimum of 4 shows up within the first 10 simulated shots every time. On Instance B, the 5-node graph, greedy from a worst-case start gets stuck at 4, while simulated annealing reliably reaches the true optimum of 5 across every seed tested.

Walking Lesson 21's four checks against this exact table: is the baseline strongest? Including SA's reliable result is what makes this fair -- showing only 'QAOA beats greedy' would already be the first failure mode. Is the metric clearly specified? Notice two different QAOA numbers are reported, expected cost and best-of-shots, because either alone would misrepresent the result. Is the size representative? Both instances are tiny, specifically for teaching -- this says nothing about hundreds or thousands of nodes.

None of the four methods wins outright across both instances and both metrics -- and that's the honest, correct conclusion, not a cop-out. Simulated annealing reliably solved the one case where greedy failed. QAOA's best-of-shots result matched the true optimum on the one instance tested, but only because its expected-value performance was propped up by concentrating most of its probability on the two optimal bitstrings -- which won't be true of every problem instance.

Chapter 6 is your capstone: pick a real combinatorial optimization problem, formulate it as a QUBO, build a hybrid workflow around it, benchmark it fairly against a classical baseline, and document the result honestly -- held to exactly this standard.
